name: SWEDEN

flag.title: Swedish Flag
flag.note: Blue field with gold Nordic cross

lead: Sweden is a long country in northern Europe. Forests cover half the land, and in summer the sun barely sets. It gave the world IKEA furniture, Spotify music and dynamite. It recycles so well that it imports rubbish for fuel. Moose roam the trees.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Sweden stretches 1,500 km from south to north. Southern farms grow strawberries. Arctic peaks stay snowy. Nearly 100,000 lakes dot the land.
Lapland lies above the Arctic Circle. In June the sun never fully sets. In January it never fully rises. Winter nights glow with green and violet northern lights.
animals: The älg, or moose, is taller than a horse. It wanders into suburbs every autumn. Sweden has around 300,000 moose.
Wolves nearly died out, but returned in the 1980s. They share the forests with bears, lynx and wolverines. In Lapland, Sámi people herd reindeer across the frozen plains.
culture: Swedes love beautiful, useful design. Minecraft and Skype started here too. Every week, Swedes take a fika, a cosy coffee-and-cake break.
At Midsommar, people dance around a flower-covered pole and eat pickled herring under a sun that won't set. On Saint Lucia Day in December, girls wear candle crowns.
history: Around 800 CE, Norse Vikings sailed east and west. They traded, raided and built settlements from Constantinople (now Istanbul) to Newfoundland (in Canada). In the 1600s, Sweden ruled much of northern Europe.
Sweden has not fought a war in over 200 years. It gave everyone free healthcare and school. It is among the happiest, most equal countries on Earth.
wows: Sweden has around 270,000 islands, mostly tiny and rocky.
Sweden imports other countries' rubbish because its rubbish-burning power plants run short.
ABBA sold over 400 million records from a country of just 10 million.
Alfred Nobel, a Swede, invented dynamite and created the Nobel Prize.
In 1967, Sweden switched from left- to right-side driving overnight at 5 a.m.
Stockholm's metro is called the world's longest art gallery, with 100 stations.
Swedish meatballs trace back to a Turkish recipe King Charles XII brought home in the early 1700s.

myths.fact: No Viking helmet with horns has ever been found. That idea came from 1800s costumes and paintings.

myths.myth: Lemmings jump off cliffs on purpose
myths.fact: They do not. The idea comes from a 1958 Disney film that faked the scene.
